what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard the recommended FY22 capital plan, which covers 13 funded projects out of the requests submitted, and took no votes beyond adjournment.
The five-year financial forecast was presented, with a school long-term staffing plan scenario; the minutes' headline notes deficits in FY23 through FY26.
The capital planning committee is to draft what it wants in a capital financial policy and send it to the Finance Committee for review.
The school budget presentation was set for March 18, with the School Committee aiming to vote the day before.
Next week's meeting will be held, and members are to email the chair agenda ideas before Monday.

why_it_matters: The capital plan decides which repairs, vehicles and equipment are paid from taxes, free cash and stabilization, and several requests were left unfunded, so those needs carry into later years.
Forecast deficits in later years point to pressure on future tax bills or services, and the school staffing scenario and salary assumptions are among the inputs that shape that outlook.
watch_next: The capital planning committee's draft capital financial policy, due to go to the Finance Committee for review.
The School Committee vote aimed for March 17 and the school budget presentation on March 18.
